entities.summary: James II of Majorca was a key figure associated with the complex web of vassalage and diplomacy in the Crown of Aragon during the 13th century. Born into a noble family, he ascended to the throne of Majorca in 1276 and became Lord of Montpellier, wielding significant influence over the region. His strategic marriages and alliances with powerful families further solidified his position, cementing his legacy as a shrewd politician and military leader. Notably, his reign was marked by the Treaty of Perpignan in 1279, which established him as a vassal of the Crown of Aragon. This event had lasting repercussions for the region, shaping the balance of power between the various noble houses and laying the groundwork for future conflicts. James II's diplomatic prowess and military successes also had a lasting impact on the region, with his successors continuing to navigate the complex landscape of vassalage and power struggles. Despite the passing of centuries, his name remains a testament to the intricate web of alliances and rivalries that defined the medieval era. The intricate dance of power and prestige that he performed has been extensively studied by historians, offering valuable insights into the complexities of medieval politics and society.
